4/// SplitMix64 hash function for deterministic random generation
5fn splitmix64(x: u64) -> u64 {
6    let mut z = x.wrapping_add(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15);
7    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9);
8    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D049BB133111EB);
9    z ^ (z >> 31)
10}
11
12/// Get deterministic +1/-1 sign from (family, bit, dim)
13fn sign_for(family: usize, bit: usize, dim: usize) -> f64 {
14    let seed = ((family as u64) << 48) ^ ((bit as u64) << 24) ^ (dim as u64);
15    let h = splitmix64(seed);
16    if (h & 1) == 1 {
17        1.0
18    } else {
19        -1.0
20    }
21}

23/// Compute SimHash LSH signatures for a normalized vector
24pub fn simhash_lsh_multi(normalized_vector: &[f32], config: &LshConfig) -> Vec<LshFamily> {
25    let families = config.families.max(1);
26    let bits = config.bits.max(64);
27    let bands = config.bands.max(1);
28
29    let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(families);
30
31    for f in 0..families {
32        let mut bool_bits = Vec::with_capacity(bits);
33
34        for b in 0..bits {
35            // Use f64 for dot product to match Python's precision
36            let dot: f64 = normalized_vector
37                .iter()
38                .enumerate()
39                .map(|(j, &val)| val as f64 * sign_for(f, b, j))
40                .sum();
41            bool_bits.push(dot > 0.0);
42        }
43
44        // Pack into hex string
45        let mut hex_chars = String::with_capacity(bits / 4);
46        for chunk in bool_bits.chunks(4) {
47            let n = (if chunk[0] { 8 } else { 0 })
48                + (if chunk.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(false) {
49                    4
50                } else {
51                    0
52                })
53                + (if chunk.get(2).copied().unwrap_or(false) {
54                    2
55                } else {
56                    0
57                })
58                + (if chunk.get(3).copied().unwrap_or(false) {
59                    1
60                } else {
61                    0
62                });
63            hex_chars.push(char::from_digit(n, 16).unwrap());
64        }
65
66        // Split into bands
67        let band_len = (hex_chars.len() / bands).max(1);
68        let band_arr: Vec<String> = hex_chars
69            .as_bytes()
70            .chunks(band_len)
71            .take(bands)
72            .map(|c| String::from_utf8_lossy(c).to_string())
73            .collect();
74
75        results.push(LshFamily {
76            family: f,
77            bits,
78            signature: hex_chars,
79            bands: band_arr,
80        });
81    }
82
83    results
84}

86/// Compute Hamming distance between two hex signatures
87pub fn hamming_distance_hex(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize {
88    let clean = |s: &str| -> String {
89        s.to_lowercase()
90            .chars()
91            .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit())
92            .collect()
93    };
94
95    let x = clean(a);
96    let y = clean(b);
97    let min_len = x.len().min(y.len());
98
99    let mut dist = 0usize;
100    for (c1, c2) in x.chars().zip(y.chars()).take(min_len) {
101        let n1 = c1.to_digit(16).unwrap();
102        let n2 = c2.to_digit(16).unwrap();
103        let xor = n1 ^ n2;
104        dist += xor.count_ones() as usize;
105    }
106
107    // Extra nibbles count as differing bits
108    dist += x.len().abs_diff(y.len()) * 4;
109    dist
110}

112/// Estimate cosine similarity from Hamming distance
113pub fn cosine_from_hamming(distance_bits: usize, total_bits: usize) -> f64 {
114    if total_bits == 0 {
115        return 0.0;
116    }
117    let p_diff = distance_bits as f64 / total_bits as f64;
118    (std::f64::consts::PI * p_diff).cos()
119}

121/// L2-normalize a vector
122///
123/// Note: Uses f32 precision throughout. For exact Python compatibility (f64),
124/// there may be tiny rounding differences (~1 bit per 256 bits in LSH signatures)
125/// due to floating-point precision. This is negligible for practical similarity matching.
126pub fn normalize_vector(vector: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
127    let magnitude: f32 = vector.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
128    if magnitude == 0.0 {
129        return vector.to_vec();
130    }
131    vector.iter().map(|x| x / magnitude).collect()
132}

134/// Compute SHA256 hash of normalized embedding.
135///
136/// This implementation matches Thor's canonical specification:
137/// 1. Quantize each value to 6 decimal places: `round(x * 1e6) / 1e6`
138/// 2. Serialize as JSON array: `[0.001234,0.005678,...]`
139/// 3. Hash the JSON string representation
140///
141/// The 6-decimal quantization eliminates floating-point jitter from:
142/// - OpenAI API non-determinism (different servers/GPUs)
143/// - Cross-platform float representation differences
144/// - Numerical precision variations
145///
146/// This ensures the SHA256 is stable and matches Thor frontend computations.
147pub fn compute_embedding_sha256(normalized_embedding: &[f32]) -> String {
148    // Quantize to 6 decimals: round(x * 1e6) / 1e6
149    let quantized: Vec<f64> = normalized_embedding
150        .iter()
151        .map(|&x| {
152            let x64 = x as f64;
153            (x64 * 1_000_000.0).round() / 1_000_000.0
154        })
155        .collect();
156
157    // Serialize as JSON array with spaces after commas (matches Python's json.dumps)
158    // Python: json.dumps([0.1, 0.2]) produces "[0.1, 0.2]" (spaces after commas)
159    // Python: Always includes ".0" for whole numbers: 1.0 not 1
160    // Rust serde_json::to_string produces "[0.1,0.2]" (no spaces) so we need to match Python
161    //
162    // Build the JSON string manually to match Python's format exactly
163    let json_parts: Vec<String> = quantized
164        .iter()
165        .map(|&x| {
166            // Format with trailing zeros removed, but keeping .0 for whole numbers
167            // This matches Python's json.dumps float formatting
168            let s = format!("{}", x);
169            // If it's a whole number and doesn't have a decimal point, add .0
170            if x.fract() == 0.0 && !s.contains('.') {
171                format!("{}.0", s)
172            } else {
173                s
174            }
175        })
176        .collect();
177    let json_str = format!("[{}]", json_parts.join(", ")); // Space after comma!
178
179    // Compute SHA256 of the JSON string
180    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
181    hasher.update(json_str.as_bytes());
182    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
183}

189    #[test]
190    fn test_normalize_vector() {
191        let v = vec![3.0, 4.0];
192        let normalized = normalize_vector(&v);
193        assert!((normalized[0] - 0.6).abs() < 1e-6);
194        assert!((normalized[1] - 0.8).abs() < 1e-6);
195    }
196
197    #[test]
198    fn test_simhash_deterministic() {
199        let v = normalize_vector(&[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]);
200        let config = LshConfig::default();
201
202        let result1 = simhash_lsh_multi(&v, &config);
203        let result2 = simhash_lsh_multi(&v, &config);
204
205        assert_eq!(result1[0].signature, result2[0].signature);
206    }

208    #[test]
209    fn test_hamming_distance() {
210        assert_eq!(hamming_distance_hex("0000", "ffff"), 16);
211        assert_eq!(hamming_distance_hex("0000", "0000"), 0);
212        assert_eq!(hamming_distance_hex("0f0f", "f0f0"), 16);
213    }

215    #[test]
216    fn test_cosine_from_hamming() {
217        // Same signature = cosine 1.0
218        let cos = cosine_from_hamming(0, 256);
219        assert!((cos - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
220
221        // Opposite signature = cosine -1.0
222        let cos = cosine_from_hamming(256, 256);
223        assert!((cos - (-1.0)).abs() < 1e-6);
224    }

229        let hash1 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v);
230        let hash2 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v);
231        assert_eq!(hash1, hash2);
232        assert_eq!(hash1.len(), 64); // SHA256 = 64 hex chars
233    }

235    #[test]
236    fn test_embedding_sha256_matches_thor_format() {
237        // Test vector that matches Thor's canonical test case
238        let v = vec![0.123456789, 0.987654321, -0.111111111];
239
240        // After quantization to 6 decimals:
241        // 0.123456789 -> 0.123457
242        // 0.987654321 -> 0.987654
243        // -0.111111111 -> -0.111111
244
245        // Expected JSON format: [0.123457,0.987654,-0.111111]
246        // This matches Thor's JSON.stringify(toFixedArray(v, 6))
247
248        let hash = compute_embedding_sha256(&v);
249
250        // Verify it's deterministic
251        let hash2 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v);
252        assert_eq!(hash, hash2);
253
254        // Verify hash length
255        assert_eq!(hash.len(), 64);
256
257        // Verify quantization eliminates jitter beyond 6 decimals
258        let v_jittered = vec![0.1234567891, 0.9876543212, -0.1111111112];
259        let hash_jittered = compute_embedding_sha256(&v_jittered);
260        assert_eq!(
261            hash, hash_jittered,
262            "Quantization should eliminate jitter beyond 6 decimals"
263        );
264    }

266    #[test]
267    fn test_embedding_sha256_quantization() {
268        // Test that values differing only beyond 6 decimals produce the same hash
269        let v1 = vec![0.123456001, 0.999999999];
270        let v2 = vec![0.123456002, 0.999999998];
271
272        let hash1 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v1);
273        let hash2 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v2);
274
275        // Both round to [0.123456, 1.0]
276        assert_eq!(hash1, hash2);
277    }

279    #[test]
280    fn test_embedding_sha256_matches_thor_reference() {
281        // These reference values are from verify_sha_match.py
282        // which implements Thor's canonical formula: sha256(json.dumps(toFixedArray(v, 6)))
283
284        // Test case 1: Simple vector
285        let v1 = vec![0.1, 0.2, 0.3];
286        let hash1 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v1);
287        assert_eq!(
288            hash1, "9a04781069052282acb2e95529c7f5bcd85149ab2ec559c550dce80b81ceb04e",
289            "Simple vector hash must match Thor's reference"
290        );
291
292        // Test case 2: High precision vector
293        let v2 = vec![0.123456789, 0.987654321, -0.111111111];
294        let hash2 = compute_embedding_sha256(&v2);
295        assert_eq!(
296            hash2, "939cac39b5886ae89213f3db06102874acf411f6c6f7021c6b33297f1d5f39ea",
297            "High precision vector hash must match Thor's reference"
298        );
299
300        // Test case 3: Sub-6-decimal jitter (both should produce same hash)
301        let v3a = vec![0.123456001, 0.999999999];
302        let v3b = vec![0.123456002, 0.999999998];
303        let hash3a = compute_embedding_sha256(&v3a);
304        let hash3b = compute_embedding_sha256(&v3b);
305        assert_eq!(
306            hash3a, "730da253c365cc40fb4b319971547d2f33b13de3469e917da1cdbd624f8b1a2a",
307            "Jitter vector hash must match Thor's reference"
308        );
309        assert_eq!(
310            hash3a, hash3b,
311            "Quantization must eliminate sub-6-decimal jitter"
312        );
313    }
